prayerExcerpt.en-US: Neglect of duty is the first sign of that self-love which ends with the loss of grace.
prayerExcerpt.pt-BR: A negligência do dever é o primeiro sinal daquele amor-próprio que termina com a perda da graça.

meta.face: An Englishman of about fifty-five, CLEAN-SHAVEN, with a fair, fresh, lightly freckled countryman's complexion reddened by the weather and a BROAD, SHORT, OPEN face — a wide, flat forehead, WIDE, rounded cheekbones, a SHORT, UPTURNED snub nose, WIDE-SET, bright light-blue eyes creased with smile lines under sandy brows, a WIDE, thin-lipped, smiling mouth, a SHORT, ROUNDED chin; sandy-red hair going grey, cut short around the tonsure; the gaze frank and warm, down toward the child.
meta.basis: No likeness from life; Wikipedia's lead image is a Victorian stained-glass window at Eastbourne. The book tells his farming of his brother's estate, his chancellorship of Oxford, his exile with St. Edmund, his feeding the poor and his firmness for the Church; Wikipedia: he died aged 56, in 1253, and the Norman cathedral had its central tower in his century and its spire only about 1402, so the card leaves the spire off. The broad, snub-nosed, freckled face is our choice, for the farmer turned bishop whom 'young and old loved'.
